before: Before this: Go lesson 3, Add numbers. You will reuse the earlier display function and value names.
A Boolean is true or false. A comparison asks a question about values; >= means greater than or equal to.
if pages >= 3 checks that comparison. Go requires braces for the block, but does not require parentheses around this condition.
When the condition is false, the else block runs instead. Here pages equals 3, so only Goal met appears.

Expected output from this example, explained rather than executed here:
```text
Goal met
```
after: A program can choose which instructions to follow. Each path is called a branch.
A condition is a question with a true-or-false answer. This kind of answer is called a Boolean. `pages >= 3` asks whether pages is at least 3.
`if` runs the instructions in its braces when the condition is true. Go needs the braces, but this condition needs no parentheses.
`else` runs its instructions when the condition is false. Only one of these two paths runs.
The screen shows `Goal met`. pages is 3, so the condition is true.
